claim: Aurora DB instances can be created in a VPC, which gives you control over who can access your Aurora databases.
question: Can Aurora DB instances run in an Amazon VPC?

values.display: Aurora DB instances can be created in a VPC

evidence.quote: Yes, Aurora DB instances can be created in a VPC. This gives you complete control over who can access your Aurora databases, including defining virtual network topologies that closely resemble traditional on-premises networks.

claim: Aurora uses SSL (AES-256) to secure connections between the database instance and your application.
question: How does Aurora secure connections between the database instance and the application?

qualifiers.scope: connections between the DB instance and the application

evidence.quote: Amazon Aurora uses SSL (AES-256) to secure connections between the database instance and your application.

claim: You can encrypt Aurora databases at rest using keys you manage through AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).
question: How do you encrypt an Aurora database at rest?

evidence.quote: You can encrypt databases at rest using keys you manage through AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).

claim: When encryption is enabled, data at rest in the underlying storage is encrypted, along with automated backups, snapshots and replicas in the same cluster.
question: What is encrypted when you enable encryption on an Aurora cluster?

values.display: automated backups, snapshots, and replicas in the same cluster

evidence.quote: When encryption is enabled, data stored at rest in the underlying storage is encrypted, along with automated backups, snapshots, and replicas in the same cluster.

claim: Encrypting an existing unencrypted Aurora instance is not currently supported; to encrypt an existing database, create a new encrypted DB instance and migrate your data into it.
question: Can you encrypt an existing unencrypted Aurora instance in place?

qualifiers.condition: FAQ states it as not currently supported

evidence.quote: Note: Encrypting an existing unencrypted Aurora instance is not currently supported. To encrypt an existing database, create a new encrypted DB instance and migrate your data into it.

claim: Aurora databases must be accessed through the database port entered on database creation.
question: Through which port must Aurora databases be accessed?

values.display: the database port entered on database creation

evidence.quote: Aurora databases must be accessed through the database port entered on database creation.

claim: Both the MySQL- and PostgreSQL-compatible editions of Aurora are HIPAA eligible.
question: Are Aurora MySQL and Aurora PostgreSQL HIPAA eligible?

evidence.quote: Yes, both the MySQL- and PostgreSQL-compatible editions of Aurora are HIPAA eligible.

claim: GuardDuty RDS Protection profiles and monitors login activity using tailored ML models to detect suspicious logins to Aurora databases.
question: Which AWS service detects suspicious logins to Aurora databases using ML?

evidence.quote: GuardDuty RDS Protection profiles and monitors login activity using tailored ML models to detect suspicious logins.

claim: There is no separate charge for Aurora replication because it is bundled into the price; you are charged on the storage your database consumes at the database layer, not the virtualized storage layer.
question: Is there a charge for Aurora replication?

values.display: Aurora replication is bundled into the price

evidence.quote: No, Aurora replication is bundled into the price. You are charged based on the storage your database consumes at the database layer, not the storage consumed in the virtualized storage layer.

claim: Every database page read operation counts as one I/O in Aurora.
question: How does Aurora count read I/O operations?

evidence.quote: Every database page read operation counts as one I/O.

claim: Pages not in memory incur read I/O charges, at 16 KB per page in Aurora MySQL and 8 KB in Aurora PostgreSQL.
question: What page size does Aurora use to count read I/Os for MySQL and PostgreSQL?

values.display: 16 KB per page in Aurora MySQL

qualifiers.condition: pages served from memory or cache are not charged

evidence.quote: Pages not in memory incur read I/O charges (16 KB per page in Aurora MySQL, 8 KB in Aurora PostgreSQL).

claim: Aurora write I/Os are counted in 4 KB units, and only redo log records (Aurora MySQL) or write-ahead log records (Aurora PostgreSQL) are written.
question: In what unit does Aurora count write I/Os, and what does it write to storage?

evidence.quote: Write I/Os: Counted in 4 KB units. Only redo log records (Aurora MySQL) or write-ahead log records (Aurora PostgreSQL) are written — Aurora never flushes dirty data pages to storage.

claim: With Aurora Standard you pay per request for I/O, while with Aurora I/O-Optimized read and write I/O operations are included at no additional charge.
question: What is the difference between Aurora Standard and Aurora I/O-Optimized for I/O charges?

evidence.quote: With Aurora Standard, you pay per-request for I/O. With Aurora I/O-Optimized, read and write I/O operations are included at no additional charge.

claim: You can switch to Aurora I/O-Optimized once every 30 days and switch back to Standard at any time.
question: How often can you switch an Aurora cluster to I/O-Optimized, and can you switch back?

qualifiers.condition: switching back to Standard is allowed at any time

evidence.quote: You can switch to I/O-Optimized once every 30 days and switch back to Standard at any time.

claim: For customers whose I/O spend exceeds 25% of their Aurora bill, Aurora I/O-Optimized can save up to 40% on costs.
question: When does Aurora I/O-Optimized save money, and by how much?

qualifiers.condition: I/O spend over 25% of the bill

evidence.quote: For customers with an I/O spend exceeding 25% of their Aurora bill, you can save up to 40% on costs.

claim: Aurora I/O-Optimized delivers improved price performance for I/O-intensive applications that need high write throughput or run analytical queries processing large amounts of data.
question: Which workloads is Aurora I/O-Optimized best for?

values.display: improved price performance for I/O-intensive applications

evidence.quote: It delivers improved price performance for I/O-intensive applications that require high write throughput or run analytical queries processing large amounts of data.

claim: Aurora I/O-Optimized works with existing Aurora Reserved Instances, and Aurora automatically accounts for the price difference between Aurora Standard and Aurora I/O-Optimized.
question: Does Aurora I/O-Optimized work with Reserved Instances?

values.display: works with existing Aurora Reserved Instances

evidence.quote: Yes, Aurora I/O-Optimized works with existing Aurora Reserved Instances. Aurora automatically accounts for the price difference between Aurora Standard and Aurora I/O-Optimized with Reserved Instances, providing even more savings on your I/O spend.

claim: Aurora I/O-Optimized does not change the price of backtrack, snapshot, export or continuous backup.
question: Does I/O-Optimized change the price of Aurora backups and snapshots?

values.display: no changes to the price of backtrack, snapshot, export, or continuous backup

evidence.quote: No. There are no changes to the price of backtrack, snapshot, export, or continuous backup with Aurora I/O-Optimized.

claim: With Aurora I/O-Optimized, the charges for I/O operations required to replicate data across Regions continue to apply.
question: Does I/O-Optimized remove the I/O charges for cross-Region replication?

evidence.quote: Yes. The charges for I/O operations required to replicate data across Regions continue to apply.

claim: A Database Savings Plan for Aurora usage can reduce costs by up to 35% when you commit to a consistent amount of usage over a 1-year term.
question: How much can a Database Savings Plan save on Aurora usage?

evidence.quote: Yes, you can purchase a Database Savings Plan for your Aurora usage and reduce costs by up to 35% when you commit to a consistent amount of usage over a 1-year term.

claim: Use the Data API for new modern applications, particularly those built with AWS Lambda that access Aurora in a request/response model.

evidence.quote: You should use the Data API for new modern applications, particularly those built with AWS Lambda that need to access Aurora in a request/response model.
